hints: Resolve each pulling force along the direction of the river (horizontal line of motion).
The components along the river are $60\cos 25^\circ$ and $50\cos 15^\circ$.
Add these two components together to find the total force in the river direction.
walkthrough:
Resolve both pulling forces along the river direction:
$$X = 60\cos 25^\circ + 50\cos 15^\circ$$

Substitute the trigonometric values $\cos 25^\circ \approx 0.906308$ and $\cos 15^\circ \approx 0.965926$:
$$X = 60(0.906308) + 50(0.965926) = 54.3785 + 48.2963 = 102.675\text{ N} \approx 103\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: To find the total force along the river, project each pulling force onto the direction parallel to the riverbanks.

The $60\text{ N}$ force is angled at $25^\circ$ to the river direction, giving a component of $60\cos 25^\circ$. The $50\text{ N}$ force is angled at $15^\circ$ on the other bank, giving $50\cos 15^\circ$:
$$X = 60\cos 25^\circ + 50\cos 15^\circ$$

Add the two parallel components:
$$X = 54.3785 + 48.2963 = 102.6748\text{ N} \approx 103\text{ N}$$

hints: Resolve forces perpendicular to the river direction: $Y = 60\sin 25^\circ - 50\sin 15^\circ$.
Calculate the magnitude of the resultant using Pythagoras: $R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2}$.
Find the angle $\theta$ to the river direction using $\tan\theta = \frac{|Y|}{X}$ and specify towards which force it acts.
walkthrough:
Calculate the perpendicular component of the resultant force, taking the side of the $60\text{ N}$ force as positive:
$$Y = 60\sin 25^\circ - 50\sin 15^\circ = 60(0.422618) - 50(0.258819) = 25.3571 - 12.9410 = 12.4161\text{ N}$$

Calculate the resultant magnitude using $X = 102.675\text{ N}$:
$$R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = \sqrt{(102.675)^2 + (12.4161)^2} = \sqrt{10542.16 + 154.16} = \sqrt{10696.32} \approx 103.4\text{ N} \approx 103\text{ N}$$

Calculate the direction angle $\alpha$ relative to the river direction:
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{Y}{X} = \frac{12.4161}{102.675} \approx 0.120926 \implies \alpha = \arctan(0.120926) \approx 6.9^\circ$$

State the final result with direction:
$$103\text{ N at } 6.9^\circ\text{ to the river direction, towards the } 60\text{ N force}$$
teacher_walkthrough: We already have the parallel component $X \approx 102.6748\text{ N}$. Now calculate the perpendicular component $Y$.

The forces pull on opposite sides of the river, so their perpendicular components subtract. Taking the direction towards the $60\text{ N}$ force as positive:
$$Y = 60\sin 25^\circ - 50\sin 15^\circ$$

Calculate the resultant magnitude $R$ using Pythagoras' theorem:
$$R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = \sqrt{(102.6748)^2 + (12.4161)^2}$$
$$R = \sqrt{10542.11 + 154.16} = \sqrt{10696.27} \approx 103.42\text{ N} \approx 103\text{ N}$$

Find the direction angle $\alpha$ with the river direction:
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{Y}{X} = \frac{12.4161}{102.6748} \approx 0.120926$$
$$\alpha = \arctan(0.120926) \approx 6.89^\circ \approx 6.9^\circ$$

Conclude clearly:
$$\text{Magnitude is } 103\text{ N at } 6.9^\circ\text{ to the river direction, towards the } 60\text{ N force}$$
